D.t: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins leads by 5.2 in the forecast and wins 86% of simulations. The cushion is about 15,241 votes; a one point swing is about 1,454 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +0.9 and D +11.4. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +8.5. Your best recent poll is Alaska Survey Research at D +8.0; your worst is Data for Progress (D) at R +4.2. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Anchorage Municipality, a projected net 36,507 votes; Juneau City and Borough, a projected net 7,369 votes; Fairbanks North Star Borough, a projected net 6,883 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Kenai Peninsula Borough, R +0.8, 9.4% of the vote; Copper River Census Area, R +5.1, 0.4% of the vote.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 69% of voters, 46 to 22, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Immigration voters, 9% of voters, 31 to 31, where a 5 point gain is worth 0.43 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins: Immigration voters 31 to 31, White voters 46 to 22, Voters who can afford daily costs 47 to 22. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.2M cash against $207K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $1.6M helping Bernadette Wilson and $1.4M helping Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins.

R.t: Bernadette Wilson trails by 5.2 and wins 14% of simulations. Closing it takes about 7,620 voters switching sides, or 15,241 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +11.4 and R +0.9. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +8.5. Your best recent poll is Data for Progress (D) at R +4.2; your worst is Alaska Survey Research at D +8.0. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Matanuska-Susitna Borough, a projected net 6,122 votes; Southeast Fairbanks Census Area, a projected net 807 votes; Kenai Peninsula Borough, a projected net 218 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Kenai Peninsula Borough, R +0.8, 9.4% of the vote; Copper River Census Area, R +5.1, 0.4% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Bernadette Wilson runs furthest behind in Fairbanks North Star Borough, Southeast Fairbanks Census Area, Kenai Peninsula Borough. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 69% of voters, 22 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Immigration voters, 9% of voters, 31 to 31, where a 5 point gain is worth 0.43 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Bernadette Wilson: 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 8 to 71, Asian and other voters 12 to 67, Independents 14 to 68. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$207K cash against $1.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Bernadette Wilson. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Cash: $1.2M in the bank against $207K for Bernadette Wilson.
